newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares weather brief Telekom storm.
newsitem.headline: German shares weather brief Telekom storm.

text.p: German shares on Wednesday weathered the storm after news that Bonn was considering selling some of its shares in Deutsche Telekom, advancing in late trade amid more signs that the risk of a U.S. rate hike is ebbing.

The 30-share DAX index ended the bourse session down 21.46 points, or 0.6 percent, at 3,573.69 points, as shares in Telekom closed down 2.3 percent at 39.20 marks, having picked up substantially from the day's lows.

But the IBIS DAX index, which tracks all-day trade in blue chip shares, advanced in after-bourse dealings on the back of a large slip in U.S. inflation in April to end up 0.82 percent at 3,588.57 points.
Early talk that its shares might be sold on the open market had sent Telekom down to a low of 38.01 marks in pre-bourse trade amid heavy trading volumes.
"That looked like a buy opportunity to me," remarked one dealer of the swift recovery in the company's share price. The shares closed IBIS trade at 39.25 marks.
Bank shares were mostly stable and heavily traded, with Deutsche Bank rising 15 pfennigs to 97.45 marks in bourse trade and ending IBIS trade at 97.17 marks.

Bankgesellschaft Berlin rose 42 pfennigs, or 1.2 percent, to 37.90 marks after announcing the start of merger talks with Norddeutsche landesbank, a fully state-owned bank. The merger would create one of Germany's largest banking groups.
There was little market reaction to the formal announcement by Deutsche Lufthansa and other airlines of their "Star Alliance" partnership agreement.
Lufthansa shares ended bourse trade down five pfennigs at 28.20 marks and advanced later to close the IBIS session at 29.02 marks.
The impact of the Telekom saga eased as the session continued as it became clear that the government would likely not sell Telekom shares on the stock market because of legal restrictions.
Even if it did, said one trader: "I think the market could well absorb a big block of Telekom shares."
Telekom has been a market favourite in the past week amid optimism for its earnings outlook for the coming years.
